experiments.name: Phase 2-α: LLM-as-parser
experiments.description: Pre-compute argument structure for LIARArg test using cloud LLM (gpt-oss-120b via Cerebras), feed via FrozenArgParserLLM into Phase 1.

parser.notes: Zero-shot. Mixed parser sources due to API limits: 65 rows from Llama-3.3-70B (HF Inference), 320 from gpt-oss-120b (Cerebras), 40 fallback. 99.5% real parse rate after backfill+retry.

parser_level_eval.method: Same in-domain test sets as v1/v2/v3, same evaluate_corpus() threshold 0.5, single Cerebras key, sequential.

vs_v3_retention_ratio.interpretation: Distilled v3 student retains 69% of teacher parsing quality on average. Highest on CDCP (formulaic), lowest on PERSPECTRUM (which defeats extractive parsing for both models).

experiments.description: Smallest distilled student. Full fine-tune on 4 gold extractive corpora.

phase1_integration_liararg.reason: 62% empty on LIARArg parse, run killed after 90 rows. Expected integration F1 near flat-RAG.

experiments.description: Data-scaling experiment. Resume v2 adapter, train 1 more epoch on 5 gold corpora (AAEC newly added).

training.method: LoRA r=16, continual from v2 adapter

partial_parse_attempt.sample_real_parse_issues: fragments like 'is not clear' as claim text
partial_parse_attempt.verdict: domain transfer failure; killed to save Mac compute

phase1_integration_liararg.reason: Small distilled student doesn't recover cross-domain transfer ability of large LLMs.

experiments.name: Day 1 ablation: direct-from-parsed-structure (no retrieval)
experiments.description: Skip Phase 1's retriever+reranker entirely. For each LIARArg test row, take Phase 2-α's parser predictions, group premises by support/attack role, feed directly to the Ollama Qwen-14B verifier. Isolates the parser's contribution from retrieval's.

comparison.interpretation: Retrieval contributes ~5x more F1 gain than parser spans alone. Phase 1 architecture's primary value is parser-driven retrieval, not parser-as-evidence. Parser knows truth direction (within-1 0.638) but not degree (6-way 0.135).

experiments.name: Phase 2-β v4: Qwen-1.5B distilled with gold + LIARArg silver + CoT
experiments.description: Fresh Qwen-1.5B + LoRA on 5 gold corpora plus LIARArg train silver-labeled by gpt-oss-120b. Silver records included CoT reasoning traces from gpt-oss-120b, and the training format string _format_target() automatically included <think>{reasoning}</think>{json} when reasoning was present — so v4 accidentally became a full CoT-aware student.

training.silver_source: gpt-oss-120b via Cerebras on 2123 LIARArg train articles

parser_level_eval_full_uncapped.note: v4 in-domain slightly regressed vs v3 (0.207) because v3 was continual from v2 (effectively 4 epochs of learning) while v4 is fresh 3 epochs. This regression is expected and the meaningful comparison is on cross-domain LIARArg integration.

liararg_parse.improvement: Dropped from 83% empty (v3) to 23% empty (v4). Silver + CoT successfully fixed the cross-domain transfer failure.

experiments.notes: Headline result: a Qwen-1.5B distilled student captures 85% of the 120B cloud LLM's 6-way F1, essentially TIES it on 3-way F1 (99% retention) and within-1 (98% retention). The architecture claim from Phase 2-α is preserved end-to-end through distillation into a locally-runnable model.

experiments.name: Phase 2-β v4: ECHR legal-domain transfer probe
experiments.description: Out-of-distribution probe of v4 on European Court of Human Rights case briefs (12,947 cases available; n=20 sampled). ECHR was never seen in training — neither in the 5 gold corpora nor in the LIARArg silver. Tests whether v4 transfers to a genuinely novel discourse style (legal argumentation).

methodology.input_construction: Concatenate all argument spans per case, truncate at 3000 chars, feed via student.predict() with max_input_len=2048 and max_target_len=2048.

proxy_gold.source: ECHR agent labels on each argument span
proxy_gold.mapping: ECHR (Court statements) -> claim; Applicant/State/Third Parties -> premise; Non-Argument -> excluded
proxy_gold.caveats: Not an argument-mining annotation. ECHR 'Court' statements are court-of-appeal-style meta-reasoning, structurally different from Politifact-style claims v4 was trained on. Span granularity also differs (ECHR: paragraph-scale units; v4 training: shorter atomic spans).

methodology.span_matching: Word-Jaccard overlap >= 0.5 between predicted and gold span text, greedy 1-1 alignment.
methodology.parser_note: REQUIRED patched _parse_output with salvage fallback. Strict parsing returned empty on 18/20 cases because v4's generation hit max_new_tokens mid-relation-generation loop, leaving JSON unclosed. Salvage recovers the claim/premise objects that were emitted before the loop pathology kicked in.

interpretation.domain_transfer: Bounded but real. v4 recovers ~10% of ECHR-annotated argument spans on a legal-domain corpus it has never seen. Every case produced non-empty output; no full failures.
interpretation.dominant_error_source: Role-schema mismatch, not extraction. v4 identifies genuine argument spans in ECHR text (e.g., 'The applicant complained that the length of his detention on remand had been unreasonable' recovered as a claim), but the role assignments are calibrated to Politifact/argument-corpora conventions, not to ECHR's court-vs-party discourse structure. Evidenced by very low claim recall (0.017) vs moderate premise F1 (0.118): v4 identifies advocacy-style spans well, court-conclusion spans poorly.
interpretation.under_extraction: v4 predicts ~140 spans total vs ~547 gold spans (~26% coverage). Consistent with ECHR's paragraph-scale annotations being coarser than v4's atomic-span training data.
interpretation.distillation_infrastructure_finding: Discovered the relation-generation loop pathology as a domain-agnostic parser-hardening concern. Patched src/phase2/student.py:_parse_output with _salvage_parse fallback so long-input cases producing malformed JSON still yield usable output. Behavior on valid JSON is unchanged (strict parse always tried first).

experiments.commentary: Not a headline number. This is a limitation-boundary probe: 'where does v4 stop transferring?' Answer: v4 shows partial transfer to genuinely OOD legal argumentation, bounded by role-schema mismatch and paragraph-vs-atomic granularity differences. The parser-salvage fix is a real code contribution independent of the transfer result.

experiments.name: Phase 2-β v4: AMPERSAND (Reddit CMV) domain-transfer probe
experiments.description: Positive-transfer probe of v4 on the AMPERSAND corpus (Chakrabarty et al. 2019, EMNLP), which annotates Reddit ChangeMyView (CMV) sentences with a 3-way component label (non-argumentative / premise / claim). CMV Reddit discussions were never seen in training — neither in the 5 gold corpora nor in the LIARArg silver. Tests whether v4 transfers to a discourse register closer to the silver (informal argumentative debate) than ECHR was.
experiments.test_set: phase2_data/raw/AMPERSAND-EMNLP2019/claimtrain.tsv, seed=42 balanced sample of 50 per class × 3 = 150 sentences

methodology.input_construction: Each AMPERSAND sentence fed directly to student.predict() with max_input_len=2048 and max_target_len=1024. No context prefix — just the sentence.
methodology.gold_labels: 0 = non-argumentative, 1 = premise, 2 = claim (per AMPERSAND paper convention)
methodology.v4_to_gold_mapping: 0 components extracted -> non; claim_components > 0 -> claim (regardless of premises); only premise_components > 0 -> premise
methodology.parser_note: Uses patched _parse_output with salvage fallback (from ECHR probe). No degeneracy issues observed on AMPERSAND — sentences are short, no relation-generation loop.

binary_is_argumentative.reading: v4 identifies 97% of argumentative sentences (recall 0.970) with 71% precision on this OOD corpus. The 30% FP rate reflects v4 over-predicting argumentativeness on fragmentary or borderline sentences, some of which arguably ARE argumentative (v4 disagreeing with annotator labels, e.g., 'You probably really do believe America is a better place' flagged as claim but labeled non-arg).

ternary_role_classification.reading: v4 systematically over-classifies as claim (recall 0.660, precision 0.351) — consistent with its training on 5 gold corpora + LIARArg silver where 'claim' was the dominant top-level extraction target. Distinguishing claim from premise on isolated single sentences is genuinely hard: human annotator agreement on this task is typically 0.40-0.55, so v4's 0.458 claim F1 is in a reasonable band. Premise F1 is weakest because sentence-scale premises look claim-like without the discourse context that identifies them as supporting some other claim.

interpretation.positive_transfer_headline: v4 achieves binary is-argumentative F1 = 0.819 with recall = 0.970 on a Reddit CMV corpus it never saw. This demonstrates that v4's argumentativeness detection generalizes as a domain-agnostic feature, not merely a within-training-distribution behavior.
interpretation.role_labeling_limitation: Ternary role labeling (macro F1 = 0.345) is bounded by the sentence-scale isolation problem: v4 was trained on paragraph-scale inputs where claim/premise distinctions are anchored by discourse structure (support/attack relations to a top-level claim). Single sentences don't give it that context, and it defaults to labeling with the dominant training target ('claim').
interpretation.compared_to_ECHR: AMPERSAND recall (0.970) vs ECHR extraction rate (9.7%). The delta is discourse-register alignment: AMPERSAND's Reddit debate register overlaps LIARArg silver's political-opinion register, while ECHR's paragraph-scale legal reasoning is structurally distant from all training data.
interpretation.two_domain_envelope: Combining ECHR (bounded transfer, 0.074 comp-F1 with proxy gold) and AMPERSAND (strong transfer, 0.819 binary F1 with real gold), v4's transfer envelope is characterized on both sides: it transfers strongly to opinion/debate-register text at sentence-to-paragraph scale, and fails on formal legal reasoning at paragraph-cluster scale.

experiments.commentary: Headline positive-transfer number: binary is-argumentative F1 = 0.819 on out-of-distribution Reddit CMV, complementing the ECHR bounded-transfer finding. Together the two probes bound v4's domain-transfer envelope on real gold labels (not proxy).

experiments.name: Phase 2-β v4: PERSUADE 2.0 (student essays) domain-transfer probe
experiments.description: Positive-transfer probe of v4 on PERSUADE 2.0 (Kaggle Feedback Prize corpus, ~26K student argumentative essays). Similar domain to AAEC (also student essays, in v4's training) but with a different corpus (Kaggle contest essays vs Stab-Gurevych 2017) and a MORE GRANULAR 7-way component schema (Lead / Position / Claim / Counterclaim / Rebuttal / Evidence / Concluding Statement). Tests whether v4 transfers across annotation schemas within the same broad domain.
experiments.test_set: ruudra1/PERSUADE via HuggingFace, persuade_corpus_2.0_test.csv, seed=42 sample of 25 essays

methodology.input_construction: Full essay text (truncated at 8000 chars) fed to student.predict() with max_input_len=2048 and max_target_len=2048.
methodology.gold_role_mapping: PERSUADE 7-way -> v4 binary: Position/Claim/Counterclaim/Concluding Statement -> claim; Evidence/Rebuttal -> premise; Lead/Unannotated -> excluded from gold.
methodology.span_matching: Word-Jaccard overlap >= 0.5 between predicted and gold span text, greedy 1-1 alignment. Same methodology as ECHR — directly comparable.
methodology.parser_note: Uses patched _parse_output with salvage fallback. Some essays did hit long generation times (400s), consistent with occasional relation-loop truncation.

interpretation.positive_transfer_result: Extraction rate 45.7% is 4.7x higher than ECHR (9.7%). v4 recovers ~half of PERSUADE's gold argumentative spans on essays it has never seen — structural proximity to training corpora (AAEC-style essays) shows through even under a different annotation schema.
interpretation.claim_detection_works: Claim F1 = 0.351 on OOD essays is competitive with v4's in-domain performance on other corpora — e.g., v3 CDCP claim F1 was 0.507 in-domain, v3 PERSPECTRUM claim F1 was 0.063. Recall 0.451 means v4 finds nearly half of PERSUADE's Position/Claim/Counterclaim/Concluding Statement spans.
interpretation.premise_schema_mismatch: Premise F1 = 0.034 driven by systematic over-prediction (228 predicted, only 5 correct). Root cause: PERSUADE's 'Evidence' is narrowly defined (specific facts, statistics, quotes supporting a claim) and 'Rebuttal' is even narrower. v4's premise concept from training is much broader (any argumentative support), so v4 predicts many spans that PERSUADE annotators labeled as Unannotated filler or Lead. This is a granularity/schema mismatch, not a v4 competence issue.
interpretation.over_prediction_pattern: v4 outputs 419 total spans (191 claims + 228 premises) vs 188 gold — 2.2x over-prediction. Same over-prediction pattern seen on AMPERSAND (30% FP on non-arg sentences) and consistent with v4's default-to-claim training bias.
interpretation.three_domain_envelope: Combining the three OOD probes, v4's transfer envelope is: AMPERSAND Reddit debate (F1 0.819 binary is-arg) > PERSUADE essays (F1 0.193 component macro, ext 45.7%) > ECHR legal briefs (F1 0.074 component macro proxy, ext 9.7%). Ordering follows discourse-register proximity to training corpora, with student essays landing in the middle (structurally similar but schema-different).

experiments.commentary: Third-domain probe with real span-level gold (not proxy like ECHR). Positions PERSUADE at the middle of the transfer envelope. Extraction rate 45.7% and claim F1 0.351 are honest positive-transfer numbers; premise F1 0.034 documents where v4's coarser schema starts to hurt.

experiments.name: Infrastructure: _parse_output salvage fallback
experiments.description: Patched src/phase2/student.py to add a lenient JSON salvage fallback when strict parsing fails. Motivated by v4's relation-generation loop pathology on long-input cases (surfaced during ECHR probe).
experiments.trigger_condition: Strict json.loads on the model's <think>-stripped output raises JSONDecodeError, or no closing brace exists.
experiments.behavior: Scans each of the four section headers ('claim_components', 'premise_components', 'citation_components', 'relations') and extracts valid {...} objects via brace-depth matching. Deduplicates relations to defuse the loop pathology. Objects that fail to parse are silently skipped rather than nuking the whole record.
experiments.impact_on_previous_runs: None. Strict parsing is always tried first, and all previously-published numbers (v1, v2, v3, v4 in-domain, v4 LIARArg integration) came from records that produced valid JSON. This patch only affects cases where strict parsing would have returned empty.
experiments.impact_on_echr_probe: 20/20 non-empty (vs 2/20 with strict parsing). Turned an apparent 'v4 fails on legal' result into 'v4 partially transfers to legal'.
